subject: Dedicated GPU pool starvation — urgent executive attention and short-term remediation
messages:
From: Marcus Young <marcus.young@trustbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Production impact: inference latency & 500s — TrustBank Dedicated pool

Sofia / Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in user-facing latency this morning (around 07:50 PT) and now are observing repeated 500s on inference endpoints behind our dedicated GPU pool. Customer-facing page load times have doubled and transaction failures are beginning to stack up. Ops attached a quick dump of queue metrics and a small diagnostic snapshot.

Can Redwood confirm whether our reserved throughput is being honored? We were told our dedicated pool would sustain 120 QPS sustained; currently we're seeing large queue depths and token-level timeouts. This is impacting TrustBank Checkout and reverting to our previous provider is not an option mid-week. We need an immediate mitigation and a timeline for full recovery.

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot_20260422.txt, queue_metrics_20260422.csv

— Marcus Young
Head of Production Engineering, TrustBank
ops@trustbank.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: inference latency & 500s — TrustBank Dedicated pool

Team —

Just received the alert from TrustBank (below). They are seeing sustained queueing and 5xx errors on their dedicated pool endpoints. Preliminary notes:
- Reported reserved throughput: 120 QPS sustained (contracted).
- Observed symptoms: queue depth > 800, token timeouts, spike in CUDA mem pressure on a subset of hosts.
- External asks: immediate mitigation + ETA to restore service level.

Jonas / David: can you confirm whether this is noisy-neighbor interference, scheduler regression, or a delivery-side throttling incident? If it is a runtime headroom issue we should consider a targeted burst expansion and hot-patch to reduce per-request tokenization overhead.

Marissa / Grace: please prepare a concise customer note for Marcus with the immediate mitigation plan and ask for permission to failover a small percentage of traffic to warmed fallback nodes while we restore headroom. We should be explicit about credits if SLAs are impacted.

I'll escalate to Jonas if we need exec support for capacity authorization.

Thanks —
Sofia
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Site Reliability <sre@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: inference latency & 500s — TrustBank Dedicated pool

Sofia / all —

Quick technical summary from the runtime team (observed in the last half hour):
- A subset of the dedicated pool nodes serving TrustBank show elevated GPU memory fragmentation and OOM-recovery cycles. That correlates with multi-tenancy spikes from a nearby capacity burst (noisy-tenant pattern).
- Scheduler logs indicate an unexpected kernel placement change at 06:58 PT caused by the auto-optimizer flag we shipped last week — it changed the default kernel selection for long sequences and increased memory working set for certain models.
- Result: effective per-request memory footprint increased ~18% at peak, pushing a narrow cohort of nodes into queueing and causing request retries that surface as 500s.

Immediate actions (can execute in the next 15–30 minutes):
1) Rollback the auto-optimizer flag on nodes in TrustBank's dedicated pool (targeted canary rollback).
2) Move 10% of TrustBank traffic to warmed overflow nodes we keep for emergency bursts (requires ops authorization).
3) Apply temporary tokenization limit policy for TrustBank routes to cap sequence length for 45 minutes.

Impact and constraints: the rollback is low risk but requires a small maintenance window (30 min). Moving traffic to overflow nodes will increase short-term cost; we should request authorization for emergency burst credits.

I'll stand by on the runbook and can start the rollback once Jonas signs off.

— David
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Young <marcus.young@trustbank.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 12:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: inference latency & 500s — TrustBank Dedicated pool

Marcus —

Thanks for flagging this. I want to be transparent about what we'll do immediately and what's coming next:
1) We will perform a targeted rollback of a runtime change affecting kernel selection — this should free memory on the impacted nodes. David's team has the runbook and is ready to execute.
2) With your permission, we'll failover 10% of requests to our warmed overflow nodes to reduce queueing while the rollback completes; we'll monitor error-rate and latency in real time and roll back traffic if you see any regressions.
3) If SLAs are missed for the hourly windows affected we will proactively apply credits per our contractual terms; we'll propose the credits after we finalize impact minutes.

Can you confirm: are you comfortable with the 10% failover for the next 45–60 minutes? If yes, we'll start step 1 immediately and inform you when the failover is live.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the severity and are treating this as priority 1.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: inference latency & 500s — TrustBank Dedicated pool

Team and Sofia —

I authorized the targeted rollback and emergency overflow for TrustBank at 16:20 PT after reviewing David's notes. Summary for execs and next steps to attach to the post-mortem:
- Root cause: auto-optimizer kernel selection change increased memory working set for long-sequence requests. Interaction with a concurrent noisy-tenant burst pushed a subset of dedicated nodes over headroom thresholds.
- Immediate remediation: rolled back optimizer flag on TrustBank nodes; diverted 10% of traffic to overflow nodes; applied temporary sequence-length cap for TrustBank routes. These actions reduced queue depth from ~800 to ~70 and lowered 5xx rate from 4.8% to 0.2% within 30 minutes.
- Customer communication: Marissa to send formal impact summary and proposed credit (estimated at 2 hours of SLA credit) by EOD.
- Follow-ups: engineering to (a) revert the auto-optimizer change to gated rollout and add regression detection, (b) add a reserved-pool isolation fence in scheduler to prevent noisy-tenant spillover, (c) update our capacity playbook to include an explicit overflow authorization path for large accounts.

I will brief CTO/COO at 17:00 PT and request an on-call budget approval for emergency overflow costs (est. $8k for the window). Please add any evidence (SRE logs, timeline, customer impact minutes) to INF-8943 before 18:00 PT.

— Jonas Weber
VP, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
